title: The Decision to Turn South
subtitle: A command decision before its military consequences
author: R.G. Cruise
phase: II — The Drive into the Soviet Interior
summary: Planned study: The German decision to redirect effort toward Ukraine, Guderian’s forces and the continuing Soviet defence of Kiev.
outlineTopics: The German operational situation in late August.
Continuing Soviet resistance and the condition of Army Group Center.
The competing German priorities of Moscow, Leningrad, and Ukraine.
Hitler's August 21 instructions rejecting the proposed immediate concentration on Moscow.
The strategic importance attached to Crimea, the Donbas, and Soviet oil supplies.
The desire to eliminate Soviet forces threatening Army Group South's northern flank.
The developing plan to use forces associated with Army Group Center in operations toward Ukraine.
The military implications for Guderian's 2nd Panzer Group.
The continued Soviet defense of Kiev and the surrounding region.
German operational coordination between the central and southern sectors.
The implications for the Moscow direction.
Soviet command decisions and attempts to preserve the Southwestern Front.
researchStatus: Editorial outline established; full narrative, document locators and the dated military situation require research.
referenceMapStatus: Collection reference only. The corresponding printed sheet date, sheet identifier and reuse conditions have not yet been verified.
chronologyNotes: The command decision precedes the later Kiev encirclement. Intended movements must be distinguished from executed advances.
